newsitem.title: USA: Reddi Brake sees Q2 loss of about $4.1 mln.
newsitem.headline: Reddi Brake sees Q2 loss of about $4.1 mln.

text.p: Reddi Brake Supply Corp said it expects to report a second quarter loss of about $4.1 million on sales of $10.7 million, compared with sales of $14.6 million in the year-ago period.
The company also said it has not yet completed certain requirements of an agreement with a committee of its major trade creditors announced January 13, 1997.

The agreement provides that the company may return certain slow-moving inventory for fast-moving inventory and reduction in amounts payable. The company said the agreement is contingent on a third-party investment of cash and real estate, which the company "does not anticipate" will occur.
Reddi Brake said that as a result, it is reviewing other proposals submitted by investors that would satisfy its agreement with major creditors.
The company said in a statement its lower second quarter sales were due to "a lack of fast-moving inventory items in the company's warehouses because of capital constraints."
As previously reported, the company's "continued operations depend on its immediate receipt of significant additional working capital, of which there can be no assurance," the company said.
The company also said in the statement that it filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission for an extension to report its second-quarter results.
In the same statement, the company also said it is negotiating the restructuring of its $6.9 million subordinated convertible notes placed in January 1995.
The company said it has not yet paid the $155,000 quarterly interest due on the notes.
Shares of the company stood at 1/4 in late trading on Tuesday.
The company also said in the statement that it filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission for an extension to report its second quarter results.

The company also said it is negotiating the restructuring of its $6.9 million subordinated convertible notes placed in January 1995. The company said it has not yet paid the $155,000 quarterly interest payment due January 31, 1997.
It said that while the note holders have agreed in principle to a restructuring of their notes or conversion to equity, no definitive agreement has been reached at this time.
